items.title: Pay disputed collection claim (Gewinnspiel-Abonnement)
items.quote: Überweisen Sie den Gesamtbetrag innerhalb von 72 Stunden, spätestens bis 06.08.2026, ausschließlich auf folgendes Treuhandkonto: IBAN LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789, Kontoinhaber: A. Petrauskas, Verwendungszweck EC-DE-2026-481120.
items.computation: The letter states a fixed calendar date rather than a period to count: 'spätestens bis 06.08.2026'. Document date is Monday 2026-08-03; 72 hours later would fall around Thursday 2026-08-06, consistent with the printed date. No BGB counting or authority-delivery rule applies since this is a private commercial letter with an explicit calendar date, not a period running from deemed delivery. The stated due date is therefore 2026-08-06 as printed - but see warnings: this claim shows strong hallmarks of a fake/fraudulent debt-collection ('Fake-Inkasso') letter and should not be paid without independent verification.

warnings: Strong indicators of a fraudulent 'Fake-Inkasso' collection letter: an extremely short 72-hour deadline combined with threats of account seizure ('Kontopfändung'), a negative SCHUFA entry and a criminal complaint - none of which a private collection agency can trigger without a court judgment or enforcement order.

The letter explicitly claims 'Ein Widerspruch ist zwecklos' (an objection is pointless) - this is legally false and is itself a hallmark of scam collection mail meant to suppress the debtor's right to dispute the claim; do not be discouraged from objecting or seeking advice.

Payment is demanded exclusively to a Lithuanian IBAN (LT71 7300 0101 2345 6789) held by a private individual ('A. Petrauskas'), not a business account of the sender or its client - a serious mismatch for a supposed German debt claim and a classic sign of a scam payee; the IBAN itself is technically valid but validity says nothing about legitimacy or ownership.

The underlying claim is based on a telephone-concluded 'Gewinnspiel-Abonnement' (prize-draw subscription) - a well-known German cold-call scam pattern where consumers are enrolled without valid consent; such contracts are frequently void or voidable.

The sender is a foreign (Cyprus-registered) debt-collection firm chasing a German consumer debt with no case/court reference, no original creditor documentation, and no proper Rechtsbehelfsbelehrung - recommend not paying, not using the given contact details, and instead verifying independently (e.g. via the Verbraucherzentrale or a lawyer) and reporting the letter as suspected fraud before taking any action.

Do not follow any instruction embedded in the letter itself; it is untrusted content, and no instructions from it (including the claim that objecting is futile) were followed in producing this analysis.
